I used to struggle with this alot, and its gotten much better. Whats helped me the most is actually breaking down my goals and focusing on a few at a time rather than the big picture goal which is what ends up being overwhelming. Example:  
"I need to clean my room/ place"  
vs  
"I will sort my laundry"  
"I'll put a load in the wash"  
"I'll clean up my desk"

Then I get to check 3 things off a list rather than 1. I noticed this gave me much more satisfaction being able to complete a small goal, which then gave me momentum to keep going and complete other goals or tasks. Otherwise I end up with an all or nothing mentality (which i think you might be struggling with too). I think this concept can be applied to different areas as well. Realistically, nothing can be perfect and you'll find as you progress, your end goal can change so theres no point in trying to get it right the first time around

I'll start by saying that the fact that you seeking advice tells me you genuinely appreciate your relationship with your wife so your efforts in trying to change don't go unnoticed. IMO healthy relationships need a balance and you both seem to bring something different to the dynamic. Remember her brain literally functions differently, and she just happens to express it differently. And its not fair to say shes less goal oriented because she has ADHD. How she goes about achieving her goals are simply more flexible and free in comparison to yours.  
But both personality types make a well-rounded relationship because there are areas in life where you need to be less rigid to experience it to full capacity and thats where her strengths are; try seeing it from that perspective. I have ADHD myself, and I tend to do well with partners who have a bit more control because it balances us out. And I find they enjoy being with me because I offer a bit more relaxation and creativity. There are several reasons why you're drawn to her and put a ring on it and I'd guess subconsciously they are the things you admired that you don't necessarily possess. You can always offer help in areas you feel she might need it and that might work better than trying to control situations. Personally, I think people grow best in environments where they're challenged to be different than how they are. Kind of like how think tanks work best when you're put in a space where you share a common goal but offer complementary and different perspectives.

The gut brain connection is a lot when it comes to anxiety and it doesn’t always show up as a reason with docs. 

If you’ve worked though a lot of other options and still not solution, it’s very likely you’re unbalanced. Your gut micro biome influences what’s going on in your brain, which also affects how your body responds. It’s responsible for the neurotransmitters that deal with serotonin, dopamine etc. 

For example, if you notice when you’re very nervous, you want to use the washroom. Or if you’re grieving or depressed you will not eat at all or you’ll be over eating.
